newsitem.title: GERMANY: FedEx adds Munich to freighter network.
newsitem.headline: FedEx adds Munich to freighter network.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said it has improved its service in Germany by linking Munich into its global freighter network.
On Tuesday the U.S. integrator started a five times a week Munich to Paris feeder flight as the return leg stopover of its new Boeing 727-200 Paris-Moscow service.
FedEx managing director Germany Antje Schuett, told Reuters in an interview: "The first freighter out of Munich is full."
Deliveries from southern German shippers such as Siemens and BMW could be collected up to 14.00 local or accepted at a new Munich airport service counter up to 16.00 local," she added.
Shipments upto 682kg as well as dangerous goods could now be accepted, she said.

FedEx released no figures on revenue or volumes carried from Germany or Europe, but Schuett noted FedEx has increased staff in Germany to 700 from 460 and the number of delivery vans to 120 from 70 over the past two years.
FedEx files daily between Frankfurt and its European hub in Paris, using either a Boeing 727-200 or 727-100, according to demand, and has a daily Paris-Cologne flight with an MD-11 aircraft.
Schuett said "We are very satisfied with our results in Germany, and, also alongside England and France, we have a key position for FedEx worldwide.
She described DHL Worldwide and UPS as the main inter-continental competitors and said FedEx had "a strong position" in the market sector which it targeted.

The Lufthansa Cargo plan to offer more logistics and door-to-door services "was a long and overdue-development" and did not surprise FedEx given the growing client demand for just-in-time services from a single supplier, she added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
